prerequisites: Proficiency in mathematical tools such as trigonometry, analytical geometry (conics and quadrics), functions of several variables, two and three-dimensional integration, and linear differential equations.
Adequate handling of concepts taught in Physics I and Mechanics I.

learning_outcomes.text: Understanding and mastery of basic concepts on the general laws of mechanics for their application to solving engineering problems: modeling, simulation, and calculation of mechanical elements and systems.
Knowledge and abilities for the calculation, design, and testing of machines.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, and is typically found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students are able to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies typically demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
Students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, abilities, and skills in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts on the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism, and their application to solving engineering problems.

syllabus_topics: Block 2. Dynamics of a rigid body
Block 3. Dynamics of a rigid body with a fixed point
teaching_methods: Theoretical approaches followed by applications in the form of exercises, problems, and laboratory practices
Detailed reading of the Study Guide
Progressive study through the basic text
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 0.8 * Final Exam (PP) + 0.15 * Continuous Assessment Test (PEC) + 0.05 * Laboratory Practices (PL). A minimum score of 3 out of 10 in the final exam is required for the PEC score to be included. If the student does not complete the PEC or its score is lower than the final exam score, they will be graded exclusively by the final exam score. Final exams are held in June, with an extraordinary retake exam in September. Passing the compulsory laboratory practices is an essential condition to pass the course, and a pass in practices is valid for five years.
